title: POC Weekly: Caching Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on caching improvements. transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-01
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Turner (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (CTO, NimbusApps), Jia Li (ML Eng), Samir Patel (DevOps), Leah Brooks (Product)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC check-in to review caching hit rates and prompt reuse strategy; focus on KV/prefix cache tuning and benchmark results.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping in. Quick roll call, then we'll go through the hit-rate numbers from last week and the small fixes Priya pushed.
[00:15] Carlos: Yep, all good here. Sound's fine.
[00:30] Priya: Great, I'll start with a quick recap of what we changed - we tightened the prefix matching to be more aggressive, added a canonical normalization pass to requests, and adjusted the KV cache TTL from 12h to 6h for staging.
[01:10] Jia: Quick Q - when you say canonical normalization, is that just whitespace/lowercase or are you normalizing placeholders and entity tokens too?
[01:25] Priya: Good question, it's a mix: whitespace, punctuation trimming, lowercasing, and a small placeholder map for common user variables (e.g., [USER_NAME] -> token). We didn't touch entity resolution yet. That step is planned next.
[02:05] Alex: Cool. So main KPI we track is effective KV + prefix hit rate and end-to-end token savings. Priya, can you share the numbers?
[02:20] Priya: Yep. Baseline (week before changes) had an overall cache hit rate ~12% across the flows we instrumented. After the normalization + prefix tweak we see a combined hit rate at 48% on staging for the targeted routes - that's across the conversational summarize and Q&A endpoint.
[02:45] Samir: Wait 48%? That's huge - is that the KV cache only or prefix + KV combined?
[02:55] Priya: Combined. Breaking it down: prefix cache is at ~35%, KV-only hits ~20% (there's overlap - when a prefix hit occurs KV isn't consulted). Effective unique request hit rate ~48%.
[03:20] Leah: Any obvious traffic skew? Like, is this only for a small subset of heavy repeat prompts?
[03:30] Priya: Mostly repeat prompts for our onboarding flows and a handful of template prompts from the product pages. We intentionally targeted those. For broad open-ended user prompts the hit rate is still low - single digits.
[04:00] Carlos: How about latency? Did the extra normalization add noticeable overhead? And does cache lookup save us on p99?
[04:10] Alex: Good point. Priya, you had a p95/p99 chart?
[04:18] Priya: I pulled the numbers. Median latency for cached responses is down ~40% compared to cold path (because we avoid full model decode). End-to-end p95 improved by ~20% overall on the instrumented routes. p99 still shows tail spikes for complex prompts that don't hit cache. Normalization added ~6-8ms per request on average - negligible compared to model latency.
[04:55] Jia: Did you also measure token savings? That's what the finance folks care about.
[05:05] Priya: Yes. Token consumption for the targeted routes dropped ~37% week-over-week on staging. That roughly maps to cost savings given the per-token billing model. We'll share the spreadsheet with exact token counts.
[05:30] Samir: On the KV side, what eviction policy are we using? LRU? TTL?
[05:38] Priya: LRU with a per-entry TTL. We shortened TTL to 6h in staging to avoid staleness; that change increased fresh hit rate slightly because of better alignment with user behavior windows.
[06:00] Carlos: I remember earlier you mentioned 'KV cash' in the doc - V1 mistyping - we want to be careful with terminology in the SOC docs.
[06:12] Alex: Noted, we'll make sure the security deck uses consistent names: KV cache, prefix cache, Redwood Optimize notes.
[06:25] Leah: Any privacy concerns with caching? Some of our prompts include PII placeholders. How are those handled?
[06:35] Alex: Good question - Redwood's recommendation is to normalize placeholders and mask PII before caching, and support TTLs along with encryption at rest. Priya, confirm what's running in staging.
[06:45] Priya: On staging, we mask obvious PII tokens and do not cache free-form user messages that contain detected PII. We also tag entries for audit. In Private deployment we'd integrate customer KMS - but for hosted pilot we're using the platform default encryption.
[07:10] Jia: How does this interact with private deployment? If we go dedicated or private, will the same cache semantics hold?
[07:22] Alex: Yes, same runtime behavior. The difference is where the cache lives (customer VPC vs Redwood-managed). Our Private customers can use their own storage and KMS. The code path is the same, just different storage backend.
[07:40] Samir: About canonical prompts - we noticed many slight variations in phrasing causing misses. Are you suggesting an aggressive dedupe that changes user wording? Concerned about changing intent.
[07:55] Priya: We're not rewriting user intent. The canonicalization is conservative: normalize whitespace, punctuation, common synonyms that we know preserve intent (e.g., "summarize" vs "give a summary"), and strip session IDs. We keep a ruleset and review potential collisions. We'll also keep a fallback path to the model when in doubt.
[08:30] Carlos: For legal/regulatory review, we need the rules documented. Can you provide that?
[08:40] Alex: Absolutely - action item. Priya will draft the canonicalization rules and a short risk assessment.
[08:50] Leah: Back to numbers - are these numbers consistent across times of day? Is hit rate falling during peak?
[09:00] Priya: There's some drop (~5-8%) during peak because of more varied user traffic, but the core templates still dominate. We can show a time-series.
[09:20] Jia: Also curious about false positives - cases where the cache returned a response that was no longer correct because context changed (e.g., dynamic tokens). Any examples?
[09:35] Priya: We found a few where the prompt included mutable state like a counter; those were excluded by the rules once detected. We added a small tag for 'stateful' prompts to bypass caching. We'll add more heuristics.
[10:05] Alex: Great. On the technical side, did you run the memory pressure tests for KV cache on the instance? Samir?
[10:12] Samir: We simulated load; with current TTL and LRU it stayed within memory for staging. But if we go to prod scale we expect to tune TTLs and maybe shard caches. Also flagged network egress for cross-AZ lookups if cache backend is remote.
[10:40] Priya: One more metric - cache fill rate. After changes, fill rate increased quickly because normalization funnels similar requests to the same key. That improved dedupe and cold start behavior.
[11:00] Jia: Regarding model fallbacks - if the cached response quality drops below threshold, do you have automatic rollback? E.g., A/B tests, or quality monitoring?
[11:10] Alex: Redwood Optimize ties evals to prompts and monitors model regressions. We can trigger alerts and automatic fallback to a safer model or to cold path generation if quality drops. That's part of the pipeline we discussed earlier.
[11:40] Carlos: Any latent tradeoff where caching biases outputs and reduces variety in user-facing features?
[11:50] Priya: Potentially; caching increases repeatable outputs for repeated prompts. For features that require diversity we keep caching off. We added per-route toggles so product teams can opt out.
[12:20] Leah: For instrumentation, can you export the raw hit logs so we can slice by customer cohort?
[12:30] Alex: Yes - we'll export the logs with identifiers removed and share the spreadsheet.
[12:40] Priya: I'll include a column for route, normalized_key, hit_type (prefix/kv), latency_ms, tokens_saved.
[13:00] Samir: On TTL strategy, are you open to adaptive TTLs based on observed frequency?
[13:10] Priya: Absolutely, adaptive TTLs are on the roadmap. For pilot we kept it static to reduce variables. Adaptive would bump TTLs for hot keys automatically.
[13:30] Jia: How about pre-warming? Can we seed cache for critical routes at deploy time?
[13:40] Alex: Yes, Redwood supports pre-warming via batch seeding; we can provide scripts. That's a good next step for onboarding flows.
[14:05] Carlos: Let's talk about benchmark plan for the next 7 days - what should we run?
[14:12] Priya: We propose: 1) canonical prompt rollout to staging; 2) 72-hour baseline vs canonical A/B; 3) run end-to-end token + latency capture; 4) surface cohort-level metrics.
[14:30] Jia: We'll do that. We want the exact script and load profile.
[14:36] Alex: I'll attach the load profiles and the benchmark sheet.
[14:40] Priya: Also note that some of our initial numbers came from a smaller subset of routes; we should expand measurement to include product pages and user-invoked flows.
[15:00] Leah: On the security side, we need the audit log format and retention policy for cached entries.
[15:10] Alex: Redwood provides audit logs - include cache actions and tags. For hosted pilot retention is default 90 days, but we can adjust for Private deployments. We'll share the security pack.
[15:30] Carlos: Does the cache store full user content or only normalized keys and responses? Need clarity for legal.
[15:40] Priya: We store the normalized key and cached response. We avoid storing raw PII and redact where detected. All stored data is encrypted.
[16:00] Samir: One operational ask - can we expose a dashboard metric for 'stale-hit' occurrences where cached response was returned but later judged stale?
[16:12] Priya: Yes, we can log a stale-hit counter and include it in the Console dashboard. We'll add it to the metrics list.
[16:30] Alex: Ok, let's go over immediate action items and owners.
[16:35] Priya: I'll prepare the canonical list and dedupe rules.
[16:40] Alex: I'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and raw logs.
[16:45] Jia: We'll run the staging pilot and push templates.
[16:50] Samir: I'll validate eviction and memory under load.
[17:00] Leah: Product will review the risk doc and canonicalization rules.
[17:20] Alex: Anything else?
[17:25] Carlos: One ask - can Redwood provide a small script to diff pre/post tokens by route? That would help our cost modeling.
[17:35] Alex: Yes, we'll add a token-diff script to the spreadsheet artifacts.
[17:45] Priya: Also, quick note: we spotted a few transcription mismatches in the previous notes where "prefix cache" was written as "pre-fix" - minor but will fix.
[18:00] Alex: Great. We'll send follow-ups. Next sync, same time next week?
[18:10] Carlos: Works for us.
[18:15] Alex: I'll send invite. Thanks everyone.

Recap / End:
- Hit rates improved from ~12% to ~48% for targeted routes after canonicalization and prefix tuning
- Token savings ~37% for the targeted routes; median latency improved substantially, p99 tail remains work in progress
- Action items assigned (see action_items)
- Next: share benchmark sheet + raw logs, canonical prompt list, run 72h A/B in staging, follow-up next week

References/shared artifacts (links):
- Benchmark spreadsheet: https://redwood.example.com/artifacts/nimbus-cache-benchmark-2026-09-01
- Canonical prompt repo (priv): https://redwood.example.com/repo/nimbus-canonical-prompts
- Security pack (SAML/KMS/SOC2 notes): https://redwood.example.com/security/nimbus-quick-pack

Questions (auto):
- Will canonicalization risk changing intent for edge cases? (Answered: conservative approach and manual review)
- Can we get raw logs filtered by cohort? (Answered: yes, Alex to share)
notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artefacts (e.g., 'KV cash'). Priya to provide canonical mapping doc.
